title: Normalized section deformation with arbitrary finite etale coefficients
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $N\geq1$ satisfy $NA=0$. Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible, where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $g:V\to S$ be smooth, separated, of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume $g$ is compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable]. Write $\mathcal I$ for the ideal sheaf of $s(S)$. The section is regular of codimension $d$; its conormal $\mathcal E=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of rank $d$. Put $\pi:N_s=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\to S$, with zero section $z$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Put
$$D=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t],$$
where this algebra is the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$ generated by $t$ and all $b/t$ with $b\in\mathcal I$. It has a map $\widetilde g:D\to\mathbf A^1_S$ and section $\widetilde s$ sending $\mathcal I/t$ to zero. The scheme $D$ is Noetherian, $\widetilde g$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$, and both $\pi$ and $\widetilde g$ are compactifiable. Its pairs at $t=1,0$ are $(g,s)$ and $(\pi,z)$, respectively.

Use the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories and compact-support adjoints [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and write $\omega_b=b^\times A$. All pullbacks are exact constant-coefficient inverse images. Let $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$, $C=s^*\omega_g$, and $F=\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}$. Both $C[-2d]$ and $F[-2d]$ are locally constant sheaves of free rank-one $A$-modules. Using the counit-defined exceptional base-change comparisons to identify fibres, there is a unique isomorphism
$$\kappa_{g,s}:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C,\qquad i_1^*\kappa_{g,s}=1_C.$$
Thus $\delta_{g,s}=(i_0^*\kappa_{g,s})^{-1}:s^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi$. These comparisons commute with arbitrary Noetherian changes of base $S'\to S$ and with separated etale maps of neighbourhoods of the section inducing a Cartesian square of centres; the comparison on normal bundles in the latter case is the induced linear isomorphism. Etale is used in the usual scheme-theoretic sense [def-weil-etale-morphism].

The precise coordinate normalization is as follows. On an etale coordinate neighbourhood of $s(S)$, take $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$ carrying $s$ to zero, and remove the other components of $e^{-1}(0)$, so the square of centres is Cartesian. The induced map of deformations is etale near the deformed section, with standard model $\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^1_S}$, whose coordinates satisfy $x_j=t u_j$. Under the comparisons of compact-support right adjoints for etale maps, $\kappa_{g,s}$ is the identity between the two pullbacks of the affine-space dualizing line; its affine-space orientation is the adjoint of the Kummer-normalized coordinate-tower counit of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. The normal-bundle orientation $z^*\omega_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}A_S(d)[2d]$ is defined by gluing the section restrictions of these affine-space adjoint orientations on bundle trivializations; invertible linear changes preserve them by [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]. Here $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$, and $A_T(d)$ is its $d$-fold tensor power, with zeroth power $A_T$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. When $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ is a valuation-ring quotient as in [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], this orientation is the section restriction of the inverse of that theorem's purity map. The formula includes $d=0$, where all standard-pair comparisons are identities.

source.place: Local construction and Gluing; finite-ring extension as in sk-thm-smooth-purity.proof.md. Section-chart normalization: sk-prop-sp-orientation-charts.proof.md, Steps 1–4. Ordinary-etale Noetherian-base formulation.

proof.text: Work locally on $S$ with an affine open $S_i$ and an affine neighbourhood $U_i$ of $s(S_i)$ in $V\times_SS_i$. Such neighbourhoods exist: start at $s(b)$, choose an affine neighbourhood in $V$, and shrink the base inside its inverse image under $s$. The smooth normal form gives a separated etale map $e_i:U_i\to\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$, with $d$ the given relative dimension. Subtract the values of its coordinates on the section, so $e_is=0$. The inverse image $P_i=e_i^{-1}(0)$ is separated etale over $S_i$ and its section is open and closed. Its complement to $s(S_i)$ is closed in $P_i$, hence closed in $U_i$. Remove that complement, and choose affine neighbourhoods and shrink the base once more if needed. Thus the centre square is Cartesian. Write $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$; then $I=JB$ and $B/I=R$. The etale algebra $B$ is flat over $P$.

source.place: Local construction, first paragraph; Stacks 054L/lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space and 024T/proposition-properties-sections

proof.text: The coordinates $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ are a regular sequence in $P$: successive quotients are polynomial rings over $R$ and multiplication by the next variable is injective by comparison of coefficients. Flat tensor exactness for $P\to B$ preserves these successive injections, so their images form a regular sequence defining the section. Tensoring $0\to J^{m+1}\to J^m\to J^m/J^{m+1}\to0$ identifies $I^m/I^{m+1}$ with $B\otimes_P(J^m/J^{m+1})$. The monomials of degree $m$ give an $R$-basis of $J^m/J^{m+1}$, and $B\otimes_PR=B/I=R$. Hence $I/I^2$ is free of rank $d$, and the canonical multiplication map $\operatorname{Sym}_{B/I}(I/I^2)\to\bigoplus_{m\geq0}I^m/I^{m+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending each basis monomial to its class. These canonical maps agree on restrictions. This proves regularity, codimension $d$ in the regular-immersion sense, local freeness of the conormal, and the global symmetric-to-graded identification.

source.place: Local construction, regular-coordinate algebra; compare Stacks 067U/lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion

proof.text:
The etale Rees chart lemma gives
$$B[t,I/t]\cong B\otimes_P R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d],\qquad x_j\mapsto tu_j.$$
Thus the induced deformation chart $D_{U_i}\to\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}$ is etale and its structural morphism is smooth of relative dimension $d$. In the full extended Rees algebra the Laurent coefficient in degree $-m$ is $I^m$, for $m>0$, and in degree $k\geq0$ it is $B$. Quotient by $t$ therefore has pieces $I^m/I^{m+1}$. Step 2 identifies its spectrum with $N_s$ and its augmentation with the zero section. Inverting $t$ gives $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$, with section $s\times1$; evaluating at $1$ gives $(V,s)$. The charts $D_{U_i}$ cover the zero fibre because their images cover the centre; together with the punctured deformation they cover $D$. Smooth permanence on the punctured part and on the etale charts proves smoothness of $\widetilde g$ of dimension $d$ everywhere.

source.place: Local construction, deformation charts and the two fibres

proof.text: Every affine ideal of the centre is finitely generated since $V$ is Noetherian: $V$ is finite type over the Noetherian $S$. If $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, its extended Rees algebra is generated by $t,f_1/t,\ldots,f_r/t$. Consequently $D\to V$ is finite type, so $D$ is Noetherian. Its map to $V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S$ is affine and hence separated. Composing with the separated base change of $g$ proves that $\widetilde g$ is separated. The bundle $\pi$ is affine, separated, smooth of dimension $d$ and finite type by its local polynomial descriptions. Every Noetherian scheme here is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: an open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact, in particular every intersection of two affine opens. Nagata therefore supplies compactifications of $\pi$, $\widetilde g$, and every separated finite-type chart map and composite used below. Their open source schemes are again Noetherian.

source.place: Local construction, finite type and compactifiability of the Rees family

proof.text:
For arbitrary, possibly nonflat, $S'\to S$, work over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset S'\times_SS_i$. Put $P'=R'[x]$, $B'=B\otimes_RR'$, $I'=JB'$. The chart $P'\to B'$ is etale and flat. Applying the Rees chart formula before and after this change gives
$$B[t,I/t]\otimes_RR'\cong B'\otimes_{P'}R'[t,u]\cong B'[t,I'/t].$$
The maps send $t$ to $t$, $b$ to $b\otimes1$, and $x_j/t$ to $x'_j/t$; likewise the conormal basis $[x_j]$ maps to $[x'_j]$. Off $t=0$ the equality is simply Laurent-polynomial base change. These canonical maps agree on restrictions and glue, proving compatibility of the entire deformation, both sections and both fibre identifications with arbitrary base change. Smoothness and relative dimension survive by smooth permanence; the base-changed closed section is still closed. Its separated finite-type structural maps are again compactifiable by Step 4 over the Noetherian $S'$.

For a separated etale map $h:V'\to V$ of neighbourhoods over $S$ with a Cartesian square of centres, on affine charts write $B\to B'$ and $I'=IB'$. Flat tensor exactness identifies $B'\otimes_BI^m$ with $I'^m$ and $B'\otimes_B(I^m/I^{m+1})$ with $I'^m/I'^{m+1}$. Tensoring the Laurent degree pieces yields $B'\otimes_BB[t,I/t]\cong B'[t,I'/t]$, inside $B'[t,t^{-1}]$. Thus the deformation map is a base change of $h$, hence etale. On the zero fibre its degree-one map is the conormal pullback isomorphism $[b]\mapsto[h^\sharp b]$; the induced symmetric-algebra map is exactly the linear isomorphism of normal bundles. The maps fix $t$ and preserve augmentations, so they preserve the sections and the fibre at $1$.

source.place: Local construction, etale maps of pairs; orientation-charts proof Steps 1–2

proof.text: Apply the ordinary-etale smooth tensor theorem to $g$, $\pi$, and $\widetilde g$. Their sources and bases are Noetherian, the maps are separated, compactifiable, smooth of dimension $d$, and the same finite ring $A$ is killed by $N$, which remains invertible on every scheme involved. Thus $\omega_b[-2d]$ is a locally constant free rank-one sheaf. Exact constant-coefficient inverse image preserves this property, giving the asserted statements for $C[-2d]$ and $F[-2d]$. No change of coefficient category is involved.

source.place: Opening paragraph: shifted locally constant dualizing lines

proof.text:
Apply counit-defined exceptional base change to $\widetilde g$ and $i_r:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$, $r=0,1$, and pull to the section. With Step 3 this gives the specified isomorphisms
$$\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C,\qquad \eta:i_0^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi.$$
The theorem applies to these closed changes of base without a flatness assumption. All pullbacks are the exact inverse images stipulated in the statement.

Etale locality of the compact-support right adjoint identifies its restriction to $U_i$ with $e_i^*\omega_{p_d}$, and on the deformation chart identifies its restriction with $\widetilde e_i^*\omega_{p_{d,\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}}$. Here the open restrictions and chart composites satisfy the Noetherian and compactifiability hypotheses by Step 4. The affine-space adjunction, compared with the Brown right adjoint by uniqueness respecting counits, identifies these dualizing objects with $A(d)[2d]$. Tate pullback then identifies both section restrictions with the corresponding pullbacks of $A_{S_i}(d)[2d]$. Smooth base change for $S_i\to S$ makes this a local isomorphism $\lambda_i:F|_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}\to a_i^*(C|_{S_i})$. Define $h_i=(i_1^*\lambda_i)\theta_i^{-1}$ and replace $\lambda_i$ by $a_i^*h_i^{-1}\lambda_i$. This gives $i_1^*\lambda_i=\theta_i$.

source.place: Local construction, affine-space adjunction and normalization

proof.text: Shift all local comparisons by $[-2d]$. Full faithfulness of degree-zero complexes identifies them with actual sheaf morphisms. On an overlap their ratio is an automorphism of $a^*C[-2d]$. In a basis it is multiplication by a section of the constant unit sheaf $A^\times$; this description is independent of the basis since $A$ is commutative. More explicitly, the constant-module Hom lemma with $P=Q=A$ identifies local endomorphisms with scalar sections; the invertible ones are precisely the units. Pulling to a geometric fibre gives an automorphism of a constant free rank-one sheaf on $\mathbf A^1_\Omega$. The ring $\Omega[t]$ is a domain, so its zero prime is dense and its spectrum is irreducible, hence connected. Sections of a constant sheaf on this connected scheme are constant. The ratio has value $1$ at $t=1$, so it is the identity on the entire fibre. Every geometric point of $\mathbf A^1_S$ lies over such a geometric fibre. Exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks imply the ratio is globally the identity: the image of its difference from identity has zero stalks and hence is zero. The same argument proves uniqueness for any two global normalized comparisons.

Sheaf-Hom gluing applies to the normalized maps and their inverses, since Step 10 proves agreement on overlaps. They glue to inverse global maps. Shifting back yields $\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C$ with $i_1^*\kappa=\theta$, unique by Step 10. At $0$ the actual section comparison is
$$\delta=\eta\circ(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1}:C\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi.$$
Under the stipulated identification by $\eta$ this is precisely the statement's formula.

source.place: Gluing, global normalized comparison and restriction at zero

proof.text:
We first check coherence of the fibre maps. For any smooth compactifiable $b$, let $b_v:v_X^*\omega_b\to\omega_{b'}$ be the mate defined by transposing the pulled-back counit through inverse compact-support exchange. The unbounded compact-support exchanges commute with composite base changes and with composition of structural maps. Mate pasting therefore gives $b_{vw}=b'_w\circ w_X^*b_v$, with the inverse-image compositors understood. For $v:S'\to S$ write $b_C:v^*C\to C'$, $b_F:\bar v^*F\to F'$ and $b_N:v^*z^*\omega_\pi\to z'^*\omega_{\pi'}$ for their section pullbacks. The two decompositions of $\bar v i'_r=i_rv$ and Step 5 give
$$\theta' i_1'^*b_F=b_Cv^*\theta,\qquad \eta'i_0'^*b_F=b_Nv^*\eta.$$
These identities establish coherence with the chosen fibre identifications; exactness of pullback alone would not suffice.

source.place: Gluing, naturality of the normalized comparison under base change

proof.text:
All maps $b_C,b_F,b_N$ are isomorphisms by exceptional smooth base change. The candidate comparison over $S'$ is
$$\kappa^v=a'^*b_C\circ\bar v^*\kappa\circ b_F^{-1}.$$
Its restriction at $1$ is $\theta'$ by Step 12, so uniqueness gives $\kappa^v=\kappa'$. At $0$, the second equality in Step 12 and the inverse formula of Step 11 give $\delta'b_C=b_Nv^*\delta$. These are the required compatibilities with arbitrary Noetherian changes of base.

For an etale map of pairs as in Step 6, the locality isomorphisms for right adjoints give $b_C:C\to C'$ and $b_F:F\to F'$ on the common bases, and the induced normal-bundle linear isomorphism gives $b_N:z^*\omega_\pi\to z'^*\omega_{\pi'}$. Compatibility of locality with the fibre comparisons follows from the same mate-pasting calculation: locality is the comparison between the composite adjunction for $Rh_!\dashv h^*$ and the compact-support adjunction for the composite structural map. Compact-support composition and base-change coherence commute these two decompositions; pasting mates yields $\theta'i_1^*b_F=b_C\theta$ and $\eta'i_0^*b_F=b_N\eta$. Thus $a^*b_C\circ\kappa\circ b_F^{-1}$ is normalized at $1$ and equals $\kappa'$ by Step 10. Restriction at $0$ gives $\delta'b_C=b_N\delta$. This proves the etale-neighbourhood compatibility with exactly the linear map of Step 6.

source.place: Local construction and orientation-charts proof Step 3, etale locality

proof.text: For the standard pair the Rees calculation is $R[t,u]$ with $x_j=tu_j$. Identify $\omega_{p_d}$ and its affine-line base change by the adjoints of the specified Kummer-normalized coordinate-tower counits. The actual trace maps commute with arbitrary Noetherian base change. Transposing their equality and comparing right adjoints by their counits gives that the exceptional fibre comparison at $1$ is the identity in these orientations. For a section chart $e_i$, locality and fibre comparison commute by the pasting calculation of Step 14. Thus the unnormalized chart map $\lambda_i$ of Step 9 already restricts to $\theta_i$ when these orientations are used, so its correction $h_i$ is the identity. Consequently $\kappa$ is precisely the identity between the two pullbacks of the affine-space dualizing line in every such chart, as asserted.

source.place: Local construction, standard model; orientation-charts proof Step 3

proof.text: On a trivializing open of $N_s$, pull the inverse of the adjoint affine-space orientation to its zero section, obtaining $z^*\omega_\pi\to A_S(d)[2d]$. On overlaps two trivializations differ by an invertible linear change of coordinates. Linear trace invariance says their coordinate-tower counits agree after this change. Uniqueness of right adjoints compatible with counits gives equality of the adjoint orientations. After section restriction they are maps between shifted sheaves, so full faithfulness and sheaf-Hom gluing give the stated normal-bundle orientation for arbitrary finite $A$. Linear isomorphisms preserve it by exactly the same equality. For coefficients in the scope of the vector-bundle-purity theorem, that theorem defines its integration by these same affine traces; its inverse purity map therefore has the same local restrictions and agrees after gluing. When $d=0$ the standard adjunction is the identity and all coordinate calculations have no variables; the claimed identities follow. If $S$ is empty all maps are unique; if $A$ is the zero ring all module sheaves vanish, and the comparisons remain unique isomorphisms.

source.place: Local construction and orientation-charts proof Step 4, linear normalization
